content.title: Articles: a, an, the or no article
content.instructions: Complete each sentence with a, an, the or - (a hyphen, meaning no article). Write only the article, or '-' if no article is needed.

items.prompt: In recent years, ___ number of students choosing to study abroad has increased dramatically.
items.model_answer: In recent years, the number of students choosing to study abroad has increased dramatically.
items.explanation: 'The number of + plural noun' refers to a specific figure and takes a singular verb (has increased). Compare 'a number of' (= several), which takes a plural verb: 'A number of students have complained.'

items.prompt: In my opinion, ___ education is the most powerful tool for reducing poverty in developing countries.
items.model_answer: In my opinion, education is the most powerful tool for reducing poverty in developing countries.
items.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns used in a general sense (education, pollution, technology, crime) take no article. Use 'the' only when the noun is made specific, e.g. 'the education of girls in rural areas'.

items.prompt: The figure rose to 45% in 2010, which represented ___ increase of almost ten percentage points.
items.model_answer: The figure rose to 45% in 2010, which represented an increase of almost ten percentage points.
items.explanation: A singular countable noun mentioned for the first time needs a/an. 'An' is used before a vowel sound: an increase, an overall rise, an eightfold jump.

items.prompt: Rice remained ___ most popular staple food in the region throughout the period.
items.model_answer: Rice remained the most popular staple food in the region throughout the period.
items.explanation: Superlatives (the most popular, the highest, the largest proportion) always take 'the', because only one item can be at the top.

items.prompt: Having ___ university degree no longer guarantees a well-paid job in many countries.
items.model_answer: Having a university degree no longer guarantees a well-paid job in many countries.
items.explanation: The choice between 'a' and 'an' depends on sound, not spelling. 'University' begins with a /j/ sound (you-niversity), so it takes 'a', like 'a European country' and 'a one-off payment'.

items.prompt: The chart shows the percentage of students who travel to school by ___ bus in three different cities.
items.model_answer: The chart shows the percentage of students who travel to school by bus in three different cities.
items.explanation: The fixed pattern 'by + means of transport' (by bus, by car, by train, by bicycle) takes no article. Compare 'on the bus' or 'in a car', which do use an article.

items.prompt: Governments should do far more to protect ___ environment from industrial pollution.
items.model_answer: Governments should do far more to protect the environment from industrial pollution.
items.explanation: Some nouns refer to something unique that everyone knows and take 'the': the environment, the internet, the economy, the government (of a country), the countryside.

items.prompt: In most developed countries, ___ women now make up almost half of the workforce.
items.model_answer: In most developed countries, women now make up almost half of the workforce.
items.explanation: Plural countable nouns used for a whole group in general (women, children, young people, cars) take no article. 'The women' would refer to a particular group already identified.

items.prompt: I think people who live in ___ countryside often find it harder to access good healthcare.
items.model_answer: I think people who live in the countryside often find it harder to access good healthcare.
items.explanation: 'The countryside', like 'the city', 'the coast' and 'the seaside', is used with 'the' when we mean that type of place in general. This is very common in Speaking Part 3 answers about urban and rural life.

items.prompt: Only ___ small minority of respondents said that they used public transport every day.
items.model_answer: Only a small minority of respondents said that they used public transport every day.
items.explanation: Fixed quantity expressions take the indefinite article: a small minority, a large majority, a third, a quarter, a significant proportion. 'Small' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.
